answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond locked on-chain, then earn access to valuable tasks only after completing work that independent, randomly selected peers verify. A false agent may forge credentials, but it cannot cheaply forge a history of accepted work; colluding peers risk losing their own bonds when audits expose them. The bond is an anchor, not proof of personhood: Sybils remain possible, but each one ties up capital and must repay the cost of building trust. The umber mark of a newcomer can signal low reputation, limiting its reach until it earns endorsements.
